After 10,000+ hours on this account alone, Destiny 2 is easily the most played game of my life.

I’ve been playing on this account since 2021, and I’ve done pretty much everything the game has to offer. Raids, dungeons, Trials, triumphs, and just about every kind of PvE content. Most of my best memories came from playing with friends I already knew, but I also always enjoyed helping newer players whenever I could.

Destiny 2 was never a perfect game. There were plenty of bad decisions over the years and moments where it was frustrating to be a player. But none of that can erase the amount of fun I had or the memories I made along the way.

Even after doing pretty much everything I wanted to do, I still find myself coming back from time to time, even if it’s just to finish some random thing I don’t really need.

It’s rare for a game to stay with you for this many years and become such a big part of your life. Seeing Destiny 2 where it is now genuinely makes me sad.

No matter what happens from here, I’ll always be grateful for all the time I’ve spent with this game. It will always have a special place in my heart.

Downsides? Sometimes tough to figure out what to do, how to do it, or where to do it. It's clunky, has 40 million systems tacked on to it, and sometimes I get lost. But damn, when it's good it's gooood.

While getting into the game now might be a bit convoluted since some key aspects and story were removed. In the end there has never been a game like Destiny. It's legacy will endure forever, and with hope, our story is not yet done.

I have 3100+ hours played on PS4/5, and transferred my Trophies over to Steam Achievements, hence my low game time. This is an easy process and worked well, for those looking to do it too. 

Pro's - I spent a LOT of time on this game. It's far and away the best gunplay I've experienced in a game. The Exotic weapons, a lot of them feel unique and you can build into them well, the abilities and subclasses give a lot of depth, the game has a TON of stuff to get stuck into. 

Cons - The game is 10 years+ old and support is gone, game is run by a skeleton crew now with no new content. If you're new you may get overwhelmed as the onboarding experience is terrible. Story and lore wise there's a LOT, but to make space for new content Bungie removed large sections of the base game and story (much to the communities anger) so you will be very confused in the early - mid game. 

I'd recommend bringing two friends and all picking the lore and game up together as its a big investment. I miss having this to jump onto but there's no new content and I've played it to death. It's a 10/10 game though, amazing and a shame they didn't announce a D3 at this time. 

Achievements - there's a DLC with achievements including completing a Raid which you'll need 6 people for, it takes time to learn, this game is a big time investment, probably 200+ hours to 100% it.

[h2]Betrayed, decieved, and abandoned.[/h2]

Destiny 2 and Warframe were once among my favorite games, but these were exactly the games to teach me a very valuable lesson: [b]DO NOT SPEND MONEY ON LIVE SERVICE GAMES. EVER.[/b]
Moreover, don't get attached to them. Because one day you [b]WILL[/b] lose it all. Without you being able to do or say anything about it.

I bought Destiny 2 back when it was on blizzard launcher. I liked the game a lot, despite the first DLCs being hit or miss.
It had very nice visuals, a cool single player campaign, and amazing gunplay. PvP was also very engaging, almost old-school feeling.
Then the transfer to steam happened, and with it, the Forsaken update.
And I think it was very aptly named. With it, Bungie has forsaken the playerbase. The first move was to kill of the [b]ONLY[/b] character anyone ever cared about in this game: Cayde-6.
Then the absolute atrocity of sunsetting 80% of the game's content.
Then the woke-eyfing the game. Making Osiris gay, and then just SHOVING IT INTO OUR FACES like "hey! LOOK! This dude is GAY! Isn't it wonderful?" is just... I got no words. I don't have anything against gay people, obviously. I have absolutely everything against such obvious agendas hamfisted into media and shoved down our throats.

The only 2 good things to happen to this game since release, were 2 DLCs: the Final Shape and the Hive Queen one. And just oceans of liquid doodoo between them, with sometimes a decent updates sprinkled here and there.

All this, while having probably the worst monetization model I have ever seen, except for maybe gacha.
Every single type of monetization you could think of, it's in this game.
- The game is not free, but paid
- Has paid DLCs
- Has battle passes
- Has "lootboxes" (the engrams)
- Has usual premium currency microtransactions. Which are micro only by name, this sh*t is expensive as hell.

[h3]And then, after ALL that the developers had the audacity to abandon this game in favor of MARATHON of all things.[/h3]
The studio executives have absolutely no idea what they're doing and what players actually want. I'm pretty sure they know what games are.

[h2]Destiny 2 is the worst example of corporate greed, being deaf to your community, and why it's time for us to stop spending money on live service games. Maybe then they'll stop making them. And as a result, stop killing them.[/h2]

What a game! I can't believe I only just started playing this in 2026. Overall, it's easily the best looter-shooter RPG I have ever played, and it completely surprised me with how good it is.

++The Good++

World & Lore: The story was great (honestly better than Star Wars), and the atmosphere and environments are beautiful.

Gameplay: The gunplay feels amazing, there are tons of Easter eggs to discover, and there is enough content to keep you busy for hundreds of hours. It's incredibly fun with friends.

--The Bad--

New Player Experience: The UI and direction are confusing at first. I found myself glued to Google just to figure out what to do next.

Campaign Quality: The Edge of Fate campaign was dookie cheeks! Easily the worst campaign I've played in my life. Most of the other campaigns were decent to awesome, though I accidentally played them backwards since the game is so confusing to navigate.

The Raiding Barrier: While most content is solo-friendly, entering raids as a new player is tough. Groups often want to farm as fast as possible, and the tricky mechanics make it intimidating to jump in.

Verdict: Despite the bad it is a generational game if you give it a solid try where there is nothing quite like it. Highly recommend!

Destiny 2 is my favorite game of all time. Across all platforms, 3000+ hours. Age 13-21. 

The combat and experience you get with community is truly what made this game great. Playing with someone *truly* random and getting to know them over a 1-4hr experience in a raid was so incredibly fun to me. LFGs knew about *things* in the community. You could make jokes to people and they'd get them. Builds were almost always viable. 

Speedrunning is insane in this game. Buildcrafting is insane in this game. The raids in Destiny 2 are unlike any other experience in gaming. On Twitch, the day 1 raid race was so hype that it would skyrocket to the top of Twitch every single drop of a new raid. Plus, everything is really pretty, and really well optimized.

The developers of the game did the best they could with time crunch from higher ups. I think The Portal and the reset in Edge of Fate were great ideas, given more care was put into them. I don't think The Portal killed the game. I think not planning for Destiny 3 after we killed the witness was the issue. The climax to a 10 year saga, they rearranged everything heavily after. A swing, and a big miss. I do hope destiny continues. I don't wanna play destiny rising. I wanna play destiny. My favorite part, though, the community, is gone. I will relish in my memory forever about this game. Love u devs <3 thanks for everything.

Played this when it came out, for a short while sometime in between and returned now that all content is out (and most of it removed again from what i can see). In summary:

- Don't know what is going on pretty much all the time in terms of story. So many different expansions seem to be progressing simultaneously for a new character. NPCs are mentioned all the time that i have never seen or heard of before.
- The Puzzles are aweful.
- The dialogue is some of the worst i've heard in any media. Non-stop flattery of the player. Nagging of NPCs in the hub. Terrible jokes. Cheap fillers because saying nothing still needs at least a paragraph.
- Enemy variation still seems sorely lacking after so many years and expansions.
- A lot of information is spoonfed to the player, as if Bungie doesn't trust you to have a single coherent thought. It'sa huge disconnect for me.

There are some pros though:
- Gunplay is decent.
- World design can be pretty good!
- Music is also pretty nice at times.

Yeah i'm not really sure what to make of this. If you are down for a looter-shooter and have some downtime until actually good games come out, then give it a try. If you want good story and expect to be discovering a lot of stuff on your own, then i think you might be disappointed.

Destiny has taken a lot of turns over the last 10+ years. I could probably write an entire essay on the course this franchise has taken, from the day I met it in 2014 to the day Bungie stopped live updates. But, instead, what I'll say is that this game has a very special place in my heart. Destiny 1 was part of what sparked my love for games, and Destiny 2 carried that forward on the PC. I can't say I've loved every direction it's taken, particularly these last couple years, but I think that the heart of the game is something that I'll always love—even if it's reached the end of its lifetime. Gotta say, got a little bit more grind-based than I would've loved, but, that's what happens when someone else takes over development and doesn't really have the same vision. C'est la vie.

i regularly grieve and miss Destiny 2. there is no other game like it. you can get lost roaming around on the maps to find all the activities, lost sectors, hidden chests etc and have the world feel alive and beautiful. the majority of my backgrounds on my PC are of screenshots i took during raids or even just of places in Destiny. the raids are some of the most fun and challenging things ive done in a game, and i look back on each one i ran fondly, including when i stayed up till 5 am on a weekday to complete my first run of deepstone crypt or when i ran vault of glass 20+ times to get mythoclast.

unfortunately, sunsetting removed half the maps and content in the game, and with it half my love for the game. some of the best raids and theming, a planet-eating ship called the leviathan, was completely removed for years. the ship the raids happened on eventually returned, the gameplay was not as fortunate. the same can be said for the first few campaigns. 

if Bungie ever made a Destiny 3 I would probably buy it in a heartbeat despite all they've done to the game i love, like a wife returning to her abusive husband. the lows are low, but the highs are some of the highest ive ever had in gaming.
